div.div: Two facts the kit stresses: (1) L2-resident streaming is 12.4x (Orin) / 14.6x (Thor) faster than DRAM. (2) L2 latency barely moved generation-to-generation (146 -> 156 ns) while L2 capacity grew 8x. Bigger L2 = more data stays resident, not resident data reached faster.

text.tspan: Two facts the kit stresses: (1) L2-resident streaming is 12.4x (Orin) / 14.6x (Thor) faster than DRAM. (2) L2 latency barely moved generation-to-generation (146 ->
156 ns) while L2 capacity grew 8x. Bigger L2 = more data stays resident, not resident data reached faster.

div.div: Legend: blue = Orin measured green = Thor measured latency = dependent-load landmark "resident read" = bandwidth when the working set fits that level. Latency rises + bandwidth falls going down; capacity rises.
